title: Face Sculpt #146 · 일본 30대 · 냉혹한 · 러시안 립 초초과장 · 둥근 베이비 페이스 · 잉크 블랙립 · P50 · 귀 금속 추
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, close-up beauty portrait. ONE woman, her head turned about forty-five degrees to her right in a three-quarter view, her eyes still looking straight into the camera, one ear and the turned cheek clearly visible, and from this angle the full projection of her lips from her face is clearly visible, framed tightly from the very top of her head down to the line of her shoulders, the frame cutting off just below them, so the weights fully hang in view. Her face is large and sharp. Mid 30s.

Subject: A real photograph of a striking adult Japanese woman — Japanese poised refined beauty light-neutral complexion with a soft peach-beige undertone and real visible pores, mid 30s, long glossy dark-brown waves swept to one side, a blurred ink-black gradient across the lids like soft smoke, a fine black liner, natural full lashes, a soft highlight on the cheekbones, ink-black glossy lips with a softly blurred gradient edge, odd-eyed with two clearly different lenses: her left eye has a vivid violet-purple coloured contact lens with a thick dark outer ring and round natural pupils, fully opaque and solidly saturated across the whole iris with no natural brown showing through, the colour bright and unmistakable, with a darker limbal ring, and her right eye has an intense crimson-red coloured contact lens with a heart-shaped pupil, fully opaque and solidly saturated across the whole iris with no natural brown showing through, the colour bright and unmistakable, with a darker limbal ring, sitting naturally on the irises and clear of the eyelids, the two eye colours both bright and clearly different from each other, a cold narrowed stare without a trace of warmth straight through the camera, brows low and still, lips pressed in a thin flat line, an icy, ruthless, merciless expression — a photograph of a real Japanese woman's face, not an illustration, not a render. She has no eyebrows at all: her brow bones are completely smooth, bare, clean skin with no hair, no drawing and no ornament, like the face of the Mona Lisa, so the whole attention rests on her eyes. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living skin with visible pores and faint peach-fuzz hairs, slightly asymmetrical with a few small natural beauty marks and freckles, never airbrushed and never smooth like plastic, real wet catchlights in the eyes, individual hair strands catching the light. Her face has been surgically sculpted far beyond her natural look, and these changes override her natural features: her lips are the star of her face (the shape, size and projection described here override the lips of her makeup, while the lip colour and finish follow her makeup and ignore any lip colour named here): lips inflated far beyond the fantasy limit: so tall that together they fill the whole space between the base of her nose and the tip of her small neat chin, the upper lip lifted so high that it nearly presses against the base of her nose, a plump heart-shaped bow with two razor-sharp towering peaks, the lower lip a gigantic, domed, glossy cushion, the whole pout projecting enormously far forward from her face like a sculpted doll mouth, the width of the mouth still in proportion to her face, every edge perfectly crisp and razor-sharp, so the lips are overwhelmingly the dominant feature of her face in this three-quarter view; mirror-glossy pink-nude with bright white highlights along the top of each lip and on the dome of the lower lip, perfectly symmetrical, sculpted and still beautiful, never duck-like, never smudged past the lip line; her nose: a very steep, sharply sculpted surgical nose: a knife-like bridge that rises steeply and sharply from the brow, a needle-pointed tip projecting well forward, and very narrow, tightly pinched nostril wings with thin, slit-like nostrils; her jawline and chin: a soft, round 'baby face' jaw: full, plump, rounded cheeks, a short, soft, rounded jawline with no sharp angles and a small, round, slightly full chin. Every feature is exaggerated but beautiful, balanced and refined, in harmony with the rest of her face, never distorted, never grotesque.

Piercings: A face fully covered with real piercings, about thirty-nine in total (not counting the hanging weights), spread over every area so that no area is empty: a single large septum ring of different sizes and shapes through the thin soft wall between the nostrils, in a short stack that ends above the upper lip; one small ring wrapping snugly around each nostril wing; one straight bar across the bridge of the nose, from just below the inner ends of the brows (well clear of the eyes) down to the middle of the nose, each with a gem cap at both ends; on each ear, one large healed opening in the earlobe holding a very thick, heavy black cast-iron ring as thick as a finger, a plain solid ring with no open tunnel, and above it sit seven pieces above the lobe: four classic round O-rings and studs along the helix rim, two studs and small bars across the upper cartilage and one in the conch and tragus; five small studs across the lower half of the forehead just above the brows in even rows, leaving the upper forehead free; three small studs on each temple bone, well clear of the eyes; four small studs along each cheekbone, well clear of the eyes. The left and right sides are balanced. The pieces are spread over the whole face in clear rows so every one reads individually, with bare skin between them; the eyes and eyelids stay clear. Henna: fine metallic gold henna mehndi line patterns of vines and dots are painted across the upper forehead near the hairline only, above the forehead studs, well clear of the eyes and brows. All the ear weights hang from the bottoms of this iron ring, and they are not counted in the piercing total: on each ear there are exactly nine separate massive weights, each of a different shape and a different metal, all of them rough, hammered, matte and unpolished, each hanging on its own thick heavy chain of the same metal as the weight: on the left ear oxidized dark copper a bell-shaped weight like a small temple bell with a flared rim on a shortest chain, rough-cast matte yellow gold a barrel-shaped weight on a shortest chain, blackened cast iron a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre on a short chain, tarnished dark silver a teardrop-shaped sinker on a medium chain, dull blue-grey lead a round bell on a medium chain, dull dark brass a hammer head on a long chain, dark patinated bronze a miniature anvil on a longer chain, dull pewter-grey tin a square-sided cowbell on a longer chain, dark patinated bronze a cube-shaped block on a longest chain; on the right ear tarnished dark silver a barrel-shaped weight on a shortest chain, blackened cast iron a pyramid-shaped lump on a shortest chain, rough-cast matte yellow gold a hammer head on a short chain, dull blue-grey lead a ship's anchor on a medium chain, oxidized dark copper a teardrop-shaped sinker on a medium chain, dull dark brass a bell-shaped weight like a small temple bell with a flared rim on a long chain, dark patinated bronze a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre on a longer chain, dull pewter-grey tin a miniature anvil on a longer chain, oxidized dark copper a round bell on a longest chain. On each ear the single iron ring carries all the weights, hanging in a staggered cluster on chains of different lengths and staggered at different heights so every weight is fully visible and none hides another. Every single weight is a massive, dense, solid lump of metal at least as big as her whole fist and clearly larger than her earlobe, rough and matte and unpolished with no shine and no delicate or thin parts; its size does NOT shrink just because there are many of them: the last weight is exactly as big, as thick and as heavy-looking as the first. Each weight alone looks like it weighs several kilograms, each chain is pulled bar-straight and taut, and at a glance every single one looks crushingly, unmistakably heavy, the chains hanging freely in the air, clear of her neck and shoulders, with even the longest chain and its weight ending no lower than the level of her collarbones, never below them and never resting on her chest or body. Because all the load is carried by one opening, the weight gently pulls each earlobe down a little into a slightly elongated, soft, healthy loop of skin, only a small natural droop that is just enough to show how heavy the weights are; the lobe never stretches long, never tears or collapses and never hangs down to her neck or shoulder, her head stays upright, and the skin stays smooth and intact, fully healed, with no tearing, no wound, no blood and no redness. The face and ear jewelry is real pastel-enamelled gold set with white pearls, pastel gemstones, hearts and stars, while the hanging weights are always rough, matte, unpolished heavy metal in mixed materials (lead, tin, gold, silver, bronze, copper, brass and iron), sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Hair: her hair is swept back behind both ears, leaving both ears, her jawline and her neck fully visible so every hanging piece is in clear view.

Lighting: MANDATORY pure pitch black void background only, absolutely NO studio backdrop NO texture NO grey NO gradient. A soft key light from the front and slightly to the side on her face and ears, so the glints on every piece of metal read clearly against her skin; a thin cool rim light along the hair and shoulders. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
